q1.boundary: The Catalog Management bounded context (catalog-management) becomes a broker boundary: its two services move from Redpanda to Apache Kafka, while ecommerce-tenant-service (store-provisioning) and the query services ecommerce-product-query-service and ecommerce-category-query-service stay on Redpanda. Every consumer x topic binding that crosses catalog-management (INBOUND or OUTBOUND) now crosses the Redpanda/Kafka boundary and must be carried by MirrorMaker 2; the INSIDE binding (ecommerce-image-service x catalog.product.events) moves with both services and needs no mirroring.

q4.must_preserve: Tenant events produced on Redpanda by ecommerce-tenant-service must keep reaching the catalog service on Kafka (flow redpanda->kafka), under the same topic name, with the group ecommerce-catalog-service continuing near its Redpanda position (translated offset) rather than skipping new tenant events. The DLQ target tenant.tenant.events.dlq must exist on Kafka because auto-create is off.

evidence.reference: INBOUND binding, producer ecommerce-tenant-service stays outside catalog-management.

q4.must_preserve: Same as for the catalog service: tenant events from Redpanda must reach the image service on Kafka via redpanda->kafka, with group ecommerce-image-service offsets translated, and tenant.tenant.events.dlq present on Kafka.

Both ProductUpdated (catalog service) and ProductImagePromoted (image service), now produced on Kafka, must be mirrored kafka->redpanda into the existing Redpanda topic catalog.product.events under the same name and partition, so the storefront product read model and image URLs keep updating. Per-partition order matters less because projections are versioned, but no producer may write to this topic on Redpanda after the switch (that would mix sources).

evidence.reference: OUTBOUND, PROMISED_AND_OBSERVED, two producers inside catalog-management.

q4.must_preserve: Attribute events from the catalog service on Kafka must be mirrored kafka->redpanda into the Redpanda topic catalog.attribute.events, so the product read model keeps attribute data current. This binding is undocumented and has no catalog promise, so only the broker attachment and config show it; it is easy to miss and must be in the allow-list.
Category events from the catalog service on Kafka must be mirrored kafka->redpanda into catalog.category.events on Redpanda, so the category read model keeps updating.

The same mirrored catalog.attribute.events on Redpanda must also keep feeding the category read model; because it has two consumer services, one mirror flow serves both, and neither may be moved off Redpanda by this change.

q5.statement: Producers are declared only, never observed: that the catalog and image services are the only writers of catalog.* topics comes from source and the event catalog, not from the broker. If anything else writes to catalog.* on Redpanda after the switch, it would not reach the image service on Kafka (no redpanda->kafka flow for those topics).

AIP never establishes delivery between brokers, and its only broker id kafka:sokol111-local is the declared id of the current broker; its rows match the Redpanda groups I read with rpk, not the Apache Kafka container. After the move, delivery over both MM2 flows must be verified with broker tools (end offsets on both sides, query-service lag on Redpanda, moved groups attached on Kafka). The move is not shown to be lossless or exactly-once: MM2 is at-least-once, so duplicates are possible after restarts.

evidence.reference: Tool description: delivery between brokers is never established; request_context.broker_ids = [kafka:sokol111-local].
